observations.text: Project is Arduino C++ (not Python despite global default). ESP32-S3 target with dual-core FreeRTOS.
Used pointer-based AsyncWebServer/AsyncWebSocket in WebSocketServer class to avoid default constructor issues. Allocated via new in begin().
AsyncTCP lib needed const on status() method — patched AsyncTCP.h:198 and AsyncTCP.cpp:1344.
DNSServer method is processNextRequest() not processNext(). Fixed wifi_manager.cpp.
Arduino .ino must not #include its own .cpp files — causes multiple definition linker errors. All code lives in .ino directly; src/ modules provide class implementations.

2026-08-08: Cloud dashboard sync stalled on live boards. Root cause = stale RTDB /devices/<id>/ota trigger from cloud-OTA experiment; on boot its md5 != NVS appliedMd5 so board ran dead downloadOTA (TLS -1000) then paused=true, halting all /latest pushes. Fix: delete stale trigger+firmware nodes from RTDB; also hardened checkOtaTrigger() to use its own fbOta connection, 10s throttle (FIREBASE_OTA_CHECK_MS), and treat null /ota as normal so empty-read GET never tears down fbdo's TLS session (commit 6fa1033).

2026-08-08: Cloud OTA via RTDB downloadOTA is a dead end (TLS code -1000 on device). /ota trigger poll kept only as cheap trigger check; real firmware delivery is via USB/tools/ota_upload.py. Ops: Arduino serial-port service holds /dev/ttyACM0 and blocks arduino-cli upload — kill PID before flashing.
